newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait urges calm ahead of stealth arrival.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait urges calm ahead of stealth arrival.

text.p: Kuwait was tightening internal security ahead of the expected arrival on Friday of U.S. stealth planes for possible attacks against former occupier Iraq, an event Baghdad has described as an act of war.

Interior Minister Sheikh Ali Sabah al-Salem al-Sabah appealed for calm and urged residents to ignore rumours about the security situation to preserve the stability of the country amid heightened tension between Iraq and the United States.
Residents reported seeing extra police and checkpoints around Kuwait City overnight. Police made thorough checks of vehicles and passengers' documents.
"We must be careful and take security measures," a Foreign Ministry official said. "We have a very, very bad experience with this (Iraqi) regime. We do not trust this regime."
"So we cannot take any chances. We will not give him a chance to destroy us," he said.
Several foreign workers in Kuwait asked the scores of reporters assembling in the Gulf state in anticipation of an imminent U.S. attack if they should transfer their savings home.
"I have about 20,000 pounds ($5,900). Should I send them home?" asked one concerned Egyptian.
An erroneous rumour swept Kuwait on Thursday that the airport was closed -- an unsubstantiated piece of gossip that is a regular feature of Kuwait's post-Gulf War flaps with Iraq.
The international airport was working normally and travel agents said incoming aircraft were crowded with passengers returning to Kuwait after summer holidays.
"The situation is calm. There is no need for fear," Sheikh Ali said in a statement published in al-Watan daily.
"The Ministry...urges citizens and residents to be cautious and take precuations and to stay calm and not listen to rumours and talks that could be used by fifth columnists (traitors)."

"All the security bodies are in a state of alert as a result of the situation," al-Watan reported him as saying. It said Sheikh Ali urged people to obey traffic regulations strictly "to avoid accidents that can result from panic and fear".

Iraq, in a fresh standoff with Washington over the expansion of a southern no-fly zone, told Kuwait on Thursday it would be committing an act of war if it allowed U.S. stealth planes to use its territory for attacks on his country.

The planes were moving into position for possible bombing raids against Iraq after Iraqi forces fired a surface-to-air missile at U.S. fighters over northern Iraq on Wednesday. Kuwaitis said they expected the planes to land around 1700 GMT.
"Iraq once again is hallucinating," Kuwaiti radio said of Iraq's threats, adding that its words were "mere insolence".
Watan daily reported separately that the government had put into operation a contigency crisis plan to clear hospital beds and forbid doctors going on leave. This could not be immediately confirmed.
A military source said the Kuwaiti military was in a state of readiness but was not on top alert. Most military personnel could still take leave if they applied for it, he added.
